samples.text:
The chart shows how the households in three income groups spend their money on food in one country in 2024.

Low income households spend most of their food money on groceries, which is 72%. Takeaway is 14%, restaurants is only 8% and work or school meals is 6%.

For middle income households, groceries is also the biggest part but it is lower, 58%. Restaurants is 18%, takeaway is 16% and work or school meals is 8%. This group spends a bit more on takeaway than the others.

High income households are different from the other groups. Groceries is only 41%, and restaurants is 32%, which is four times more than low income group. Takeaway is 15% and work or school meals is 12%, and this is the highest for this category.

Overall, groceries is the biggest part of food spending for all groups, but when the income is higher, people spend less percentage on groceries and more on restaurants. Takeaway is almost same for all three groups, between 14% and 16%.
samples.why: All figures accurate · overview present but late · group-by-group listing with repetitive structures · limited vocabulary · recurring agreement errors plus article and word-choice slips that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
The bar chart compares how households in three different income groups divided their spending on food between groceries, restaurants, takeaways and work or school meals in 2024.

Overall, groceries accounted for the largest share of food spending in all three groups, but this share decreased as income rose. In contrast, the proportion spent on eating in restaurants increased considerably with income, while spending on takeaway food was relatively similar across the groups.

Low-income households spent almost three-quarters of their food budget (72%) on groceries, compared with 58% for middle-income families and just 41% for the wealthiest group. The opposite pattern was seen for restaurant meals, which made up only 8% of spending for low-income households, but 18% for those in the middle group and 32% for high-income households, four times as much as the lowest group.

Takeaway food represented a fairly stable share, ranging from 14% to 16%, with the middle-income group spending slightly more than others. Meanwhile, work and school meals accounted for the smallest proportions, although the figure rose steadily from 6% among low earners to 8% and then 12% in the highest income bracket.
samples.why: Clear overview of how spending shifts with income · key features highlighted with accurate comparisons · logical progression and varied linking · good collocations · one or two minor slips.

samples.text:
The chart illustrates how food expenditure was distributed across four categories by low-, middle- and high-income households in one country in 2024.

Groceries were the largest component of food spending for every group, but their share fell markedly as income increased. Conversely, the more households earned, the greater the proportion they devoted to restaurant meals and, to a lesser extent, work or school meals, while takeaway spending varied little.

For low-income households, groceries absorbed 72% of the food budget, leaving relatively little for other categories: 14% went on takeaways, 8% on restaurants and 6% on work or school meals. Middle-income households spent a smaller share on groceries (58%) and more than twice as much, proportionally, on restaurants (18%), with takeaways and work or school meals at 16% and 8%.

The contrast was sharpest in the high-income group. Here, groceries accounted for only 41% of food spending, while restaurants made up 32%, four times the share recorded for low-income households. Work or school meals also reached their highest level, at 12%, double the proportion for the lowest income group. Takeaways, by contrast, remained remarkably consistent, representing between 14% and 16% of spending in all three groups.
samples.why: Key features skilfully selected around the income gradient · clear overview · accurate figures and derived ratios · sophisticated cohesion · wide, precise vocabulary · complex structures used accurately throughout.
